findings.title: Null dereference when event has no destinationCalendar and location is Google Meet
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when `destinationCalendar` is null or empty. The next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. The old code was `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, which was safe. Any Google Meet booking where neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar now throws a TypeError in `EventManager.create`, instead of falling back to Cal Video. It should be `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Video references lose their credentialId
findings.body: The old code was `credentialId: isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId`. The new code is `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`, so non-calendar (video) results now get `credentialId: undefined`. `BookingReference` rows for video meetings are saved without a credential. `handleCancelBooking` only deletes the meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set, so cancelling a booking silently skips deleting the Daily/Zoom/etc. meeting. The non-calendar branch should still use `result.credentialId`.

findings.title: Hangout-link patch uses undefined calendarId when falling back to primary
findings.body: `selectedCalendar` is now `undefined` when no destination calendar matches the credentialId. The insert falls back with `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` still passes the raw `calendarId: selectedCalendar`. Previously `selectedCalendar` defaulted to `"primary"`. The patch that writes the Meet link into the description now fails or targets the wrong calendar whenever the fallback is used.

findings.title: Destination calendars without a credentialId no longer route to their externalId
findings.body: The selected calendar is now found only by `cal.credentialId === credentialId`. In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, destination calendars without a `credentialId` take the else branch and call `createEvent(c, event)`. That is a legacy but still supported path. For those, the destination's `externalId` is never matched, so the event is created on `"primary"`. Before this change the destination's `externalId` was always used. Users who selected a non-primary calendar will now have events land on their primary calendar.

findings.title: Dead/incorrect fallback lookup in updateEvent and deleteEvent
findings.body: The fallback is `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. In the else branch `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the find compares against a falsy value and effectively never matches (it returns `undefined`). The old code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`. Updating or deleting a reference that has no stored `externalCalendarId` now hits an undefined calendar (update) or `primary` (delete) instead of the destination calendar. The same pattern appears in `deleteEvent` (~line 317).

findings.title: Multi-host creation uses the first host's calendar id with every host's credential
findings.body: `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now calls `createEvent(credential, event, ...)` once per destination, using that destination's credential. But the same `event.destinationCalendar` array is passed each time. Office365 (and Lark) always take `[mainHostDestinationCalendar]`, the first entry, and ignore the credential/destination being processed. For the second host's credential, it POSTs to `/me/calendars/<first host's calendar id>/events` with the second host's token. That fails (404) or targets the wrong calendar. Only the Google service was updated to select by `credentialId`, so collective events for non-Google hosts are still not handled.

findings.title: CalDAV/Apple createEvent filters on the first host's calendar for every host's credential
findings.body: `calendars` is listed with the current credential, then filtered to `c.externalId === mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` where `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is always the first array entry. When EventManager invokes this service with the second host's credential, none of that account's calendars match the first host's externalId. The filter yields an empty list, `Promise.all([])` resolves, and `createEvent` returns a 'successful' result without creating anything. The second host silently gets no event.

findings.title: Unrelated change inverts the slug condition when creating an organization
findings.body: The original was `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`. It is now `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, which drops the negation. With team billing enabled, the slug is now written immediately although only `requestedSlug` should be set until payment. With billing disabled, the organization is created with no slug at all. This is unrelated to the PR's purpose and appears to be an accidental regression in organization creation.

findings.title: Team members' destination calendars are dropped when the organizer has none
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is then a no-op, so collective hosts' calendars are never added. This is the exact scenario the PR targets (other hosts having calendars). Build the array first (`[...main, ...teamDestinationCalendars]`) instead of pushing into a possibly-null value. Also, only `destinationCalendar[0]` is connected to the Booking row, so any flow that rebuilds the event from the DB later sees at most one calendar.

findings.title: Unrelated loadUsers rewrite changes selected fields and error behavior
findings.body: The `loadUsers` refactor is not related to destination calendars. It removes `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the dynamic-group user query. Any downstream code reading `user.organization?.slug` for dynamic bookings will now get undefined or a type error. It also now throws for an empty `dynamicUserList`, and the surrounding try/catch turns that into a generic 500 'Unable to load users', where it previously fell through to normal 'no users' handling. It also adds `firstName`/`lastName: ""` to team members, which are not part of the `Person` type. These behavior changes should be separated from this fix or justified.

findings.title: Recurring-cancel branch now runs once per calendar reference and only handles the first ref per booking
findings.body: The code now iterates over every calendar reference. Inside that loop, the recurring branch deletes events for every calendar credential across all `updatedBookings`, using `updBooking.references.find(...)`, which takes only the first calendar reference. With N calendar references per booking (the new multi-host case), the same deletion runs N times, producing duplicate API calls. Meanwhile the other hosts' references are never targeted, because `find` returns only the first and only the user's own credentials are iterated. The recurring branch should be hoisted out of the per-reference loop and iterate all references.

findings.title: Flows that rebuild the event from the DB only get a single destination calendar
findings.body: Only `destinationCalendar[0]` is persisted on the Booking. Confirmation, Stripe/PayPal payment webhooks and similar flows rebuild `evt.destinationCalendar` as a one-element array (booking's or organizer's calendar). For collective events that require confirmation or payment, `EventManager.create` runs later with only the main host's calendar, so the other hosts never receive the calendar event. The multi-host fix therefore only works for immediately-confirmed bookings.

findings.title: Webhook payload shape for destinationCalendar changes from object to array
findings.body: `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` is spread directly into webhook payloads. Changing it from a single object to an array silently changes the public webhook contract (BOOKING_CREATED, CANCELLED, REJECTED, etc.). Existing subscribers that read `payload.destinationCalendar.externalId` will break. The e2e test was adjusted to match, and null/`[]` are now used inconsistently across events. The payload should be mapped back to the old shape or the change documented as breaking.

findings.title: No tests for the new multi-destination create/update/cancel logic
findings.body: The PR changes `destinationCalendar` to an array across about 20 files and adds new branching (credential lookup from DB, per-reference updates and deletes, per-credential Google calendar selection). The PR checklist states no tests were added. The regressions listed above (null deref on Meet fallback, lost video credentialId, undefined calendarId) would be caught by basic unit tests of `EventManager.create`/`updateAllCalendarEvents` and `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent`.
